<description>
While looking into #36759 I discovered `-notorcontrol` did the opposite of what would be expected from it and I then checked for similar issues in other init options. There are several more where `-nofoo` does something surprising including one of them crashing the node.

This PR attempts to fix all these surprising behaviors while also keeping things as simple as possible and just change behavior to something that makes sense harmless in the context of the option. Fixes that use a common approach for the fix are grouped together into a commit even if the options included themselves may have no relation at all.

| Commit | Problematic options behavior | Fix approach |
|---|---|---|
| [mempool: Reject cluster limits below 1](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/512773d111daaa4330c873ed5889b9ef511f6e3a) | `-nolimitclustercount` hits an assertion in `TxGraph` on the first mempool transaction. `-nolimitclustersize` rejects every transaction. | Reject values below 1 at startup. |
| [args: Make negation a no-op for options that are off by default](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/5d2ddcae41522a0651e20476b7481ea2e50a6fcb) | `GetArg()` returns `"0"` for a negated option. The `-no*notify` options run the command `0`, `-nosigner` uses `0` as signer, `-noi2psam` fails startup and `-norpcpassword` sets the password to `0`. Opt-in because options like `-noonion` and `-noblockfilterindex` depend on reading `"0"`. | New opt-in flag `NEGATE_TO_DEFAULT` makes `GetArg()` return the default. |
| [init: Read -cjdnsreachable and -help as booleans](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/08b4f855104b7ef25b82d66447b9e502c9bef5e9) | `-cjdnsreachable=0` and `-nocjdnsreachable` turn CJDNS on. `-nohelp` prints the help. | Use `GetBoolArg()` instead of `IsArgSet()`. |
| [args, wallet: Treat empty -blocksdir and -walletdir as unset](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/cd5bfc823063f5d06e8a15180ba05e2afc7506fb) | `-noblocksdir` writes block files relative to the working directory. `-nowalletdir` fails startup. | Fall back to the default directory, like `-datadir` does. |
| [init: Disable the automatic onion service with -notorcontrol](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/faf0a220338cbff2e045f0535635590f2d33fbe2) | `-notorcontrol` connects to `0.0.0.0:9051`, which reaches a local Tor. | Set `-listenonion=0`. |
| [init: Disallow negating options where it has no meaning](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/4b181fd471f2826659e000439f10345a483309f4) | `-nobantime`, `-nocheckblocks`, `-nomaxreceivebuffer`, `-nomaxsendbuffer` and `-nomaxtipage` read as 0, the opposite of what the user asked for. | Fail at startup with `DISALLOW_NEGATION`. |

`-nomempoolexpiry` has a similar kind of problem. It evicts transactions as soon as the next one arrives. I left it out because #36540 already is open and addresses this.
</description>

<commits>
512773d111 mempool: Reject cluster limits below 1

-limitclustercount=0 or -nolimitclustercount passed the upper bound check and triggered an assertion in TxGraph when mempool sanity checks are enabled, while -limitclustersize=0 or -nolimitclustersize made every transaction fail with a misleading error. Reject both at startup.

5d2ddcae41 args: Make negation a no-op for options that are off by default

GetArg() returns "0" for a negated option, so -noblocknotify, -nowalletnotify, -nostartupnotify and -noalertnotify ran the command "0", -nosigner used "0" as the signer command, -noi2psam failed at startup and -norpcpassword set the RPC password to "0" instead of using cookie authentication. Add a NEGATE_TO_DEFAULT flag that makes GetArg() return the default instead and use it for these options as well as -rpcuser and -torpassword. The flag is opt-in because other options such as -noonion and -noblockfilterindex rely on reading "0".

08b4f85510 init: Read -cjdnsreachable and -help as booleans

Both were checked with IsArgSet(), so -cjdnsreachable=0 and -nocjdnsreachable made CJDNS reachable, contradicting the -rpcallowip error that tells users to set -cjdnsreachable=0, and -nohelp printed the help text. Use GetBoolArg() instead.

cd5bfc8230 args, wallet: Treat empty -blocksdir and -walletdir as unset

Both were checked for being set rather than for an empty path, so -noblocksdir and -blocksdir= wrote block files relative to the working directory while the block index stayed in the datadir, and -nowalletdir and -walletdir= failed at startup. Fall back to the default directory like -datadir already does.

faf0a22033 init: Disable the automatic onion service with -notorcontrol

-notorcontrol made the node connect to the Tor control port at "0", i.e. 0.0.0.0:9051, which reaches a local Tor on most systems. Set -listenonion=0 instead and reject combining it with -listenonion=1, like -listen=0 does.

4b181fd471 init: Disallow negating options where it has no meaning

-nobantime, -nocheckblocks, -nomaxreceivebuffer, -nomaxsendbuffer and -nomaxtipage read as 0, which is the opposite of what the negation suggests: bans expire immediately, all blocks are checked, buffers are minimal and the node never leaves initial block download. Reject them at startup instead.
</commits>

{
 "summary": "Fixes counterintuitive and buggy behavior when passing negated options (such as -nofoo or -foo=0) across several startup arguments. Depending on the option, negation previously caused assertions in the mempool graph, execution of a command named '0', setting RPC passwords to '0', writing block files to the working directory, or connecting to local Tor ports. The PR introduces opt-in flags to either return default values or disallow negation entirely at startup, and switches several boolean flags from checking argument existence to evaluating boolean values.",
 "problem": "Bitcoin Core's argument parsing translates negated options into \"0\" by default. When options take string commands, directories, or numeric limits, setting -nofoo causes unintended side effects such as -nolimitclustercount triggering a TxGraph assertion on the first transaction, -norpcpassword setting the password to \"0\", -notorcontrol connecting to 0.0.0.0:9051, -noblocksdir writing blocks relative to the working directory, and -nobantime causing bans to expire instantly.",
 "card": "Negating startup arguments using -nofoo or -foo=0 frequently produces surprising or broken behavior because the argument parser sets negated values to the string \"0\". This leads to crashes such as -nolimitclustercount hitting an assertion in TxGraph, security and behavioral bugs like -norpcpassword setting the RPC password to \"0\" instead of using cookie auth, -notorcontrol attempting to connect to a local Tor control port at 0.0.0.0:9051, and -noblocksdir writing block files relative to the current working directory. This pull request adds opt-in mechanisms to return default values or disallow negation at startup, switches boolean checks to GetBoolArg, and rejects invalid zero limits. It fixes multiple user-facing configuration traps across mempool, wallet, networking, and RPC startup settings.",
